questions.q: The angle between the straight lines, whose direction cosines $l, m, n$ are given by the equations $2l + 2m - n = 0$ and $mn + nl + lm = 0$, is:
questions.solution:
Given equations of direction cosies

$2ℓ + 2m - n = 0 . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . \left(i\right)$
$mn + nℓ + ℓm = 0 . . . . . . . . . . . . . . \left(ii\right)$
$ℓm + n ( ℓ + m ) = 0$

From equation $\left(i\right)$

$n = 2\left(ℓ + m\right)$
$ℓm + 2 ( ℓ + m{)}^{2} = 0$
$2{ℓ}^{2} + 2{m}^{2} + 5ℓm = 0$

Dividing by ${m}^{2}$ on both sides
$2{\left(\dfrac{ℓ}{m}\right)}^{2} + 2 + 5\left(\dfrac{ℓ}{m}\right) = 0$
Let $\dfrac{ℓ}{m} = t$
$2{t}^{2} + 5t + 2 = 0$

$2{t}^{2} + 4t + t + 2 = 0$

$\left(t + 2\right)\left(2t + 1\right) = 0$
$t = - 2, - \dfrac{1}{2}$

Case 1

$\begin{array}{ll}\dfrac{ℓ}{m} = - \dfrac{1}{2}\end{array}$

$\begin{array}{ll}m = - 2ℓ\end{array}$, $n = - 2ℓ$

$( ℓ, - 2ℓ, - 2ℓ ) ⇒ ( 1, - 2, - 2 )$

Case 2

$\dfrac{ℓ}{m} = - 2$

$ℓ = - 2m, n = - 2m$

$\left(- 2m, m, - 2m\right)$$⇒ \left(- 2, 1, - 2\right)$

$cos\theta = \dfrac{1 \times \left(- 2\right) + \left(- 2\right) \times 1 + \left(- 2\right) \times \left(- 2\right)}{\sqrt{{1}^{2} + {\left(- 2\right)}^{2} + {\left(- 2\right)}^{2}}\sqrt{{\left(- 2\right)}^{2} + {1}^{2} + {\left(- 2\right)}^{2}}}$

$cos\theta = \dfrac{- 2 - 2 + 4}{9} = 0$

$\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

questions.q: If the length of the perpendicular drawn from the point $P\left(a, 4, 2\right), a > 0$ on the line $\dfrac{x + 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 3}{3} = \dfrac{z - 1}{- 1}$ is $2\sqrt{6}$ units and $Q\left({\alpha}_{1}, {\alpha}_{2}, {\alpha}_{3}\right)$ is the image of the point $P$ in this line, then $a + \mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{3}{\alpha}_{i}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let a point on the line $\dfrac{x + 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 3}{3} = \dfrac{z - 1}{- 1} = \lambda$ be

$M\left(2\lambda - 1, 3\lambda + 3, - \lambda + 1\right)$

and the DR's of the line are $\left<2, 3, - 1\right>$

The DR's of line joining the points $\left(2\lambda - 1, 3\lambda + 3, - \lambda + 1\right)$ and $\left(a, 4, 2\right)$ will be

$\left<2\lambda - 1 - a, 3\lambda - 1, - \lambda - 1\right>$

Now its perpendicular to the given line, so$\left(2\lambda - 1 - a\right)2 + \left(3\lambda - 1\right)3 + \left(- \lambda - 1\right)\left(- 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ 4\lambda - 2 - 2a + 9\lambda - 3 + \lambda + 1 = 0$

$⇒ 14\lambda - 4 - 2a = 0$

$⇒ 7\lambda - 2 - a = 0 ⇒ 7\lambda - 2 = a$

and,

${\left(2\lambda - 1 - a\right)}^{2} + {\left(3\lambda - 1\right)}^{2} + {\left(\lambda + 1\right)}^{2} = {\left(2\sqrt{6}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ {\left(5\lambda - 1\right)}^{2} + {\left(3\lambda - 1\right)}^{2} + {\left(\lambda + 1\right)}^{2} = 24$

$⇒ 35{\lambda}^{2} - 14\lambda - 21 = 0$

$⇒ \left(\lambda - 1\right)\left(35\lambda + 21\right) = 0$

For, $\lambda = 1; a = 5$

i.e. $M ≡ \left(1, 6, 0\right)$

As $Q\left({\alpha}_{1}, {\alpha}_{2}, {\alpha}_{3}\right)$ is the image of point $P$

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{{\alpha}_{1} + 5}{2} = 1; & \dfrac{{\alpha}_{2} + 4}{2} = 6; & \dfrac{{\alpha}_{3} + 2}{2} = 0\end{cases}$

$⇒ \begin{cases}{\alpha}_{1} = - 3; & {\alpha}_{2} = 8; & {\alpha}_{3} = - 2\end{cases}$

Hence, $a + {\alpha}_{1} + {\alpha}_{2} + {\alpha}_{3} = 8$

questions.q: Let the position vectors of two points $P$ and $Q$ be $3\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$, respectively. Let $R$ and $S$ be two points such that the direction ratios of lines $PR$ and $QS$ are $\left(4, - 1, 2\right)$ and $\left(- 2, 1, - 2\right)$, respectively. Let lines $PR$ and $QS$ intersect at $T$. If the vector $\overset{\to}{TA}$ is perpendicular to both $\overset{\to}{PR}$ and $\overset{\to}{QS}$ and the length of vector $\overset{\to}{TA}$ is $\sqrt{5}$ units, then the modulus of a position vector of $A$ is :
questions.solution:
$P\left(3, - 1, 2\right)$

$Q\left(1, 2, - 4\right)$

$\overset{\to}{PR} ‖ 4\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{QS} ‖ - 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$

Dr's of normal to the plane containing $P, T$ and $Q$ will be proportional to :

$\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 4 & - 1 & 2 \\ - 2 & 1 & - 2\end{cases}\right| = 4\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

$∴ \dfrac{ℓ}{0} = \dfrac{m}{4} = \dfrac{n}{2}$

For point, $T$ : $\overset{\to}{PT} = \dfrac{x - 3}{4} = \dfrac{y + 1}{- 1} = \dfrac{z - 2}{2} = \lambda$

$\overset{\to}{QT} = \dfrac{x - 1}{- 2} = \dfrac{y - 2}{1} = \dfrac{z + 4}{- 2} = \mu$

$T ≡ \left(4\lambda + 3, - \lambda - 1, 2\lambda + 2\right)$

$Q ≡ \left(2\mu + 1, \mu + 2, - 2\mu - 4\right)$

$4\lambda + 3 = - 2\mu + 1 ⇒ 2\lambda + \mu = - 1$

$\lambda + \mu = - 3 ⇒ \lambda = 2$

and $\mu = - 5, \lambda + \mu = - 3 ⇒ \lambda = 2$

So point $T: \left(11, - 3, 6\right)$

$\overset{\to}{OA} = \left(11\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}\right) \pm \left(\dfrac{2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}}{\sqrt{5}}\right)\sqrt{5}$

$\overset{\to}{OA} = \left(11\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}\right) \pm \left(2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$

$\overset{\to}{OA} = 11\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}$ or $9\overset{^}{i} - 5\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$

$\left|\overset{\to}{OA}\right| = \sqrt{121 + 1 + 49} = \sqrt{171}$ or $\sqrt{81 + 25 + 25} = \sqrt{131}$

questions.q: For real numbers $\alpha$ and $\beta \ne 0,$ if the point of intersection of the straight lines $\dfrac{x - \alpha}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 1}{3}$ and $\dfrac{x - 4}{\beta} = \dfrac{y - 6}{3} = \dfrac{z - 7}{3}$ lies on the plane $x + 2y - z = 8,$ then $\alpha - \beta$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Given, $\dfrac{x - \alpha}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 1}{3}$ and $\dfrac{x - 4}{\beta} = \dfrac{y - 6}{3} = \dfrac{z - 7}{3}$ lies on the plane $x + 2y - z = 8$.

Let $\dfrac{x - \alpha}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 1}{3} = ∅$

and $\dfrac{x - 4}{\beta} = \dfrac{y - 6}{3} = \dfrac{z - 7}{3} = q$

Any point on the first line can be considered as $\left(ϕ + \alpha, 2ϕ + 1, 3ϕ + 1\right)$

and a point on the second line can be $\left(q\beta + 4, 3q + 6, 3q + 7\right) .$

For intersection of the lines $ϕ + \alpha = q\beta + 4 . . . \left(1\right)$

$2ϕ + 1 = 3q + 6 . . . \left(2\right)$

$3ϕ + 1 = 3q + 7 . . . \left(3\right)$

For $\left(2\right) \text{ and } \left(3\right)$ $ϕ =1, q =- 1$

So, from $\left(1\right)$ $\alpha + \beta = 3$

Now, point of intersection is $\left(\alpha + 1, 3, 4\right)$

It lies on the given plane, therefore, $\alpha + 1 + 2 \times 3 - 4 = 8 ⇒ \alpha = 5$

$⇒ \beta = - 2$ from $\alpha + \beta = 3$

Hence, $\alpha - \beta = 5 - \left(- 2\right) = 7$

$⇒ \lambda = 5\sqrt{3}$
